Demolition That Reads the Ground Before It Reads the Structure

c: Richmond Hill sits on ground that behaves differently depending on where you are in the city, and that shapes how a demolition job actually gets planned. Around Mill Pond and the town’s original streets, it’s a shed or a small deck coming down carefully behind a century home, protected the way heritage properties deserve. In Bayview Hill and Beverley Acres, it’s larger pools and structures on bigger lots, cleared with grounds and driveways protected throughout. Through Oak Ridges and the newer subdivisions closer to the moraine, it’s the standard job with one extra layer of attention — work kept inside the approved footprint, drainage respected, nothing disturbed that shouldn’t be near protected land. And along the Yonge corridor’s older side streets, it’s ordinary fence and shed demolition, no different from anywhere else in the city. The 700+ five-star reviews behind Live Junk Free consistently mention the same thing: the crew clearly understood the ground they were working on, whichever part of the city it was.
